stack.tokenFormat: W3C Design Tokens (DTCG) 2025.10: 10 *.tokens.json files behind a resolver with sets foundation and semantic and one modifier, theme (light default, dark)

outOfScope: scripts/generation: demo CVs stand in for documents received from outside; their colours are the document's own (AGENTS.md, Conventions: the design system governs the app's UI, src/ and .storybook/, only)

parts.summary: Roles are named by purpose in kebab-case in both themes, and one mapping from id to class and variable (DESIGN.md, Overview: Reading the tokens) is enforced by the contract check and the token-classes lint.
Roles alias the palette or carry a recorded rule, code reads only roles, and the contract names the roles of every component in src/components.
The tokens parse as DTCG 2025.10 through Terrazzo, both themes define the same 24 roles, and both stylesheets are built by Terrazzo behind a --check staleness gate and an edit-denying hook.
Every colour role carries its definition as $description in both themes, and DESIGN.md holds only the rules for using the tokens, citing ids, with no values and no definitions.

gates.does: Resolves both themes with @terrazzo/parser and fails when a palette entry is an alias, a role neither points to the palette nor carries a derived rule, a derived value differs from what its rule gives, the themes' roles or rules differ, or a text style's family or weight is a literal. It reads the rule from $extensions.cv-screener.derived, which is why the plugin's check-tokens.mjs flagged primary-hover, primary-pressed, surface-panel and on-surface-subtle as literals.

tool.name: scripts/design-tokens/tokenSource.ts via npm run design:export and npm run design:lint

gates.does: Terrazzo parses the resolver and every token file against DTCG 2025.10 and runs its recommended validation rules; a parse or validation error fails the build

tool.name: tz build (Terrazzo 2.7.1), inside npm run design:export

gates.does: Fails a token or group name that is not kebab-case

tool.name: Terrazzo core/consistent-naming: set lint.rules to { ...RECOMMENDED_CONFIG, "core/consistent-naming": ["error", { format: "kebab-case" }] } in terrazzo.config.ts

gates.does: Reports a colour role or derived token without $description

tool.name: Terrazzo core/descriptions with ignore for palette.*, font.*, motion.*, breakpoints.*, containers.*

gates.does: Fails front matter keys other than version, name, description, imports and components; an imports path other than the resolver; and a contract entry that states a value, reads the palette or names an unknown token. The @google/design.md linter then checks references and contrast in both themes. It does not yet check backticked ids in the prose, or that every component in src/components has a contract entry.

tool.name: scripts/design-tokens/designDocument.ts (contractProblems) and @google/design.md lint, via npm run design:export and npm run design:lint; extend with prose-id resolution and component coverage

gates.does: Fails a class that names no token, an arbitrary value, a modifier on a token utility, a palette variable, and a hex or literal colour function in src/**/*.{ts,tsx} and .storybook/**/*.tsx (scripts/generation is outside the design system, AGENTS.md). It does not read CSS, so a colour function over a role in src/styles/theme.template.css passes unchecked.

tool.name: ESLint design/token-classes and design/no-raw-color (scripts/design-lint/rules), strict in lint:strict; add a CSS check for colour functions over roles in src/styles/*.css

gates.does: Builds into a temporary folder and fails when tokens.generated.css or theme.generated.css differs from the committed file; the agent's PreToolUse hook denies an edit to either
Runs lint:strict, design:export -- --check and design:lint on every push, so a commit made with --no-verify or without the hooks installed still fails

tool.name: CI workflow running the existing npm scripts (CI=true makes the design lint strict, scripts/design-lint/plugin.mjs)
